correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the n-dependent exponential clock model with strictly positive rates, unique continuous sample ordering and uniform neighboring ratios n*r_{n,i}→a(i/n) where a is bounded continuous and may vanish. For i<j the exact two-clock race probability is lambda_j/(lambda_i+lambda_j)≤(C/n)^(j-i), so the expected number of inversions at gaps≥2 is at most n(C/n)^2/(1-C/n)=O(n^-1). Excluding them, adjacent inversions cannot touch (else transitivity makes a gap-two inversion) and inversion sets determine the full permutation. The exact chronological race probability for a length-k decreasing run is ≤R_n^k; disjoint clock blocks factor, giving domination of each size-k Laplace inclusion-exclusion term by C^k/k!. Neighbor-free subsets factor, neighboring subsets count O_k(n^(k-1)); Riemann summation of (1-exp(-f(i/n)))r_i gives ∫a(1-exp(-f)). Dominated summation yields the spatial Poisson Laplace functional. Full inversion and parity limits follow with O(n^-1) rare long-inversion error. For geometric r, sequential race selection gives exactly product_{k=2}^n[(1-r)/(1-r^k)]; nr→∞ case follows by n/2 independent odd-index adjacent comparisons. Independently recomputed exact identity and pair probabilities n=2..7 from independent enumeration. All-size convergence is analytical, not inferred from enumeration.

value.rationale: A natural complete asymptotic description of a noisy sorting regime: not merely convergence of a count, but the marked error locations, exact permutation support, parity, zero-error probability and sharp geometric recovery transition. This identifies precisely when exponential-race rankings become reliable and how sparse errors arise. The spatial point process and full permutation refinement are mathematically useful even though their constituent race identities are standard.
